about.title: Personal Injury Help in Corte Madera, California
about.longDescription: Corte Madera is a small town, but its roads carry a steady flow of traffic every day — US-101, Tamalpais Drive, and Paradise Drive all see regular use by commuters, shoppers heading to the Village, and residents just running errands. Public records show 48 injury collisions in the most recent year, with 61 people hurt. Reporting patterns show these crashes tend to cluster on Wednesdays between 5 and 7 p.m., likely tied to evening commute traffic on US-101 Northbound and the surrounding corridors. None of these crashes resulted in a traffic death that year, but injuries — from whiplash to broken bones — can still upend daily life, work, and finances. If you were hurt in one of these collisions, or in a fall, dog bite, or other accident in Corte Madera, LawProactive can help. Attorneys in our network work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless you recover money. Reaching out costs you nothing and helps you understand your options sooner rather than later.

whyChoose.title: What You Should Know Before You Wait

items.title: The Clock Is Ticking
items.desc: California law generally gives you two years from the date of injury to file a personal injury claim. If a government entity was involved, that window can shrink to as little as six months, so it pays to act early.

items.title: Partial Fault Won't Shut You Out
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, meaning you can still recover damages even if you were partly responsible for the accident. Your compensation is simply reduced by your share of fault, not eliminated.

items.title: No Cap on What You Can Recover
items.desc: For ordinary injury claims in California, there's no legal cap on non-economic damages like pain and suffering. That means your compensation isn't artificially limited by a statutory ceiling.

items.title: You Pay Nothing Upfront
items.desc: Attorneys in our network work on contingency, so there's no fee unless you win your case. This lets you get legal help without worrying about hourly rates or retainers.

items.question: How long do I have to file a personal injury claim in Corte Madera?
items.answer: In most cases, California law gives you two years from the date of your injury to file a claim. If your accident involved a government agency or entity, that deadline can be as short as six months. It's best to speak with an attorney as soon as possible to make sure you don't miss your window.

items.question: What if I was partially at fault for my accident?
items.answer: California uses a pure comparative fault system, which means you can still recover compensation even if you share some blame for the accident. Your total recovery is reduced by your percentage of fault, but it isn't barred entirely. An attorney can help assess how fault might affect your specific claim.

items.question: Where do crashes tend to cluster in Corte Madera?
items.answer: Public collision records show that reported crashes in Corte Madera tend to occur more often on Wednesdays between 5 and 7 p.m., with notable counts along US-101, Tamalpais Drive, Paradise Drive, and US-101 Northbound. These are simply patterns in the public record, not a judgment about any particular road.

items.question: Is there a limit on how much I can recover for pain and suffering?
items.answer: No — in ordinary personal injury cases in California, there's no statutory cap on non-economic damages such as pain and suffering. The amount depends on the specifics of your case, including the severity of your injuries and how they've affected your life.
